claims.text: Classification places organisms into groups using features they share. A useful diagnostic feature separates one group from the others being considered.

verification.method: Original subject authoring; requires semantic and source verification.

claims.text: Use several relevant structural features rather than a single superficial resemblance such as colour or habitat.

verification.method: Original subject authoring; requires semantic and source verification.

claims.text: In the binomial system, a species name has two parts: the genus name followed by the specific name. The genus begins with a capital letter and the specific name with a lower-case letter.

verification.method: Original subject authoring; requires semantic and source verification.

claims.text: The complete two-part name identifies the species. Different species may share a genus, so the specific name alone is not a complete species name.

verification.method: Original subject authoring; requires semantic and source verification.

claims.text: A hierarchical classification contains broad groups divided into progressively smaller groups: kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus and species.

verification.method: Original subject authoring; requires semantic and source verification.

claims.text: Organisms placed in the same smaller group share the broader groups above it, while organisms in one broad group need not belong to the same species.

verification.method: Original subject authoring; requires semantic and source verification.

claims.text: A dichotomous key uses successive pairs of contrasting statements, with one applicable choice at each step. Each choice leads to another pair or to an identification.

claims.text: A virus has genetic material enclosed by a protein coat. It is non-cellular: it is not made of cells and is not a single cell.

verification.method: Original subject authoring; requires semantic and source verification.

claims.text: Inside a host cell, the virus genetic material carries the instructions used to make new virus particles. The protein coat surrounds and protects that material.

verification.method: Original subject authoring; requires semantic and source verification.

claims.text: Viruses carry genetic material and are replicated within suitable host cells, which supplies arguments for associating them with life.

verification.method: Original subject authoring; requires semantic and source verification.

claims.text: They lack cellular organisation and independent metabolic activity, and cannot be replicated without host cells; these support treating them as non-living.

verification.method: Original subject authoring; requires semantic and source verification.
